page: Microsoft Azure HX176-48rs is an instance within the High Performance Computing family, engineered for tightly coupled, memory-intensive scientific and technical workloads. Based on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs. A defining hardware attribute is its extreme memory provisioning, supplying 1408.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 29.33 GB of memory per core. The instance also features integrated high-speed interconnect capabilities, supporting RDMA networking alongside Premium Storage compatibility.

For local I/O requirements, the instance includes 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on high-capacity memory retention, specialized networking, and CPU execution. While the full physical hardware chassis is built around a 176-core footprint, this specific configuration restricts CPU exposure to 48 dedicated vCPUs while retaining access to the massive 1408.0 GB memory pool.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance is structured for workloads constrained by memory capacity and memory bandwidth rather than massive core parallelization. Consuming 1408.0 GB with only 48 active cores delivers an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio, avoiding the software licensing overhead often associated with higher vCPU counts. Conversely, applications that require dense compute threads or GPU acceleration will find the configuration underutilized.

The Azure HX176-48rs is well targeted for memory-bound high-performance computing, large-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), complex financial modeling, and distributed scientific simulation codes requiring low-latency RDMA communication.
